::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** June 2 [1893?]  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS Mrs Clare Roels/112
:::

My dear [C C](people/person_329.qmd) 
We cannot find your porcupine, I think he must be shut up in a MS.  Susan, the cook informed me yesterday that she is going to marry in July, rather frantic for she can only get through easy work here with [Bessie](people/person_359.qmd)’s help however I am glad to be spared the break down that there will be- and Bessie has a sister who will probably come so all will most likely do well, those Collins grandchildren being all of the ‘old retainer’ kind.[^1]

I found the [Higher Religious Education](organizations/other_48.qmd) wanting to know about giving lectures to the [Reading Unions](organizations/other_211.qmd), which they were asked to do- so I wrote to [Mrs Chester](people/person_1682.qmd).  I was attacked at once for not coming to luncheon!  The young ladies were away so they forgot to ask me.  I settled the [M in C](organizations/other_82.qmd) business with [Mrs Sumner](people/person_1381.qmd)   You must be glad to leave the real summer heat in London

your affte
C M Yonge

I wish I could find the Porcupine.  How remarkably your correspondent spells.

---

[^1]: The cook at Elderfield during the 1891 census was Elizabeth Savage (b. Eling 1836/7), but she does not seem to have been one of the Collins grandchildren, so this letter probably dates from some years later.
